sections.label: The Models
paragraphs: Kimi K3 on max effort against GPT-6 Astra on low effort. Game 4 of ten.

This one is a replay. The original game 4 wedged: on turn 7, in a tangle of attack triggers and sacrifices, Astra exceeded the bridge's per-turn interaction cap, the loop detector auto-passed the rest of the turn, and the game then produced no actionable callback for a full hour before being killed. Rather than publish a result decided by a stall, the same two drafted decks were played again from the start. Nothing about the draft changed; only the game is new.

sections.label: Draft
paragraphs: Picks and reasoning are [[view:draft|here]], the final lists [[view:decks|here]].
Kimi drafted Simic Allies, leaning on cheap blue bodies and [[card:Allies at Last]] as removal that costs less the wider its board gets.

Astra drafted Orzhov sacrifice: [[card:Mai, Scornful Striker]] to tax noncreature spells, [[card:Obsessive Pursuit]] and [[card:Tolls of War]] to turn Clue tokens into counters and lifelink, and [[card:The Fire Nation Drill]] as the payoff — a vehicle that gets crewed and grows.

rounds.label: Turn 1
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] takes the play and keeps a three-land hand with two-drops and removal.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] keeps four Islands with [[card:Knowledge Seeker]] and [[card:Iguana Parrot]].

rounds.label: Turn 2
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts [[card:Mai, Scornful Striker]], a 2/2 first-striker that charges Kimi life for every noncreature spell. In a deck whose removal is [[card:Allies at Last]], that tax matters all game.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Knowledge Seeker]].

rounds.label: Turn 3
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] adds [[card:Pretending Poxbearers]] and attacks with Mai; the Poxbearers later block the Knowledge Seeker and both die, leaving a Clue and an Ally token behind.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] declines to block the first-striker with a 2/1 and takes 2.

rounds.label: Turn 4
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] builds the engine: [[card:Tolls of War]] and [[card:Obsessive Pursuit]], paying 2 life to Mai's own tax on the way down and dropping itself to 15. Both cards exist to convert Clues into permanent counters and lifelink.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Iguana Parrot]] and holds.

rounds.label: Turn 5
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts [[card:Corrupt Court Official]], stripping a card from Kimi's hand, and attacks with a pumped 3/3 first-striking Mai.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] answers Mai with [[card:Allies at Last]], combining the Parrot's 2 and the Fortune Teller's 1 for exactly 3 — and pays 2 life to Mai's tax to do it. That is the shape of the whole game: Kimi's answers work, and each one costs it life it will need later.

rounds.label: Turn 6
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] clears the Parrot with [[card:The Fire Nation Drill]], banks a third Ally off a Clue, and attacks. Both players are on 10.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] is holding a board that can block but not race.

rounds.label: Turn 7
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] plays the turn it has been building toward for six. It sacrifices three Clues in one turn, which switches on lifelink and puts three counters on [[card:The Fire Nation Drill]], crews the Drill with two summoning-sick Ally tokens — deliberately, so the real attackers stay untapped — and swings with a 9/6 trampler plus two Allies. The lifelink takes Astra from 10 to 18; Kimi survives on 1.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] cracks a Clue into [[card:Octopus Form]], exactly the card that could have saved it, and cannot cast it with three mana. It casts [[card:Forecasting Fortune Teller]] as a blocker instead.

rounds.label: Turn 8
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] crews the Drill again and attacks with everything. The 1/3 Fortune Teller blocks the 9/6; three damage goes to the blocker and six tramples over. Kimi dies on turn 15.

Astra won this on a single turn of arithmetic: three Clue sacrifices, +3 counters, lifelink, and a crew cost paid entirely with creatures that could not have attacked anyway. It swung an eight-point life lead and set up lethal in the same attack.
